title: Amity Infra Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & 5 Others
coram: Arvind Kumar Mishra-I, J. & Om Prakash Tripathi, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed as withdrawn; petitioner did not press the Clause 4.9 conversion challenge
headnote: A developer's writ challenging the amendment of Clause 4.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — converting single-point connections into multiple-point connections — was listed with the similar Maxbills Construction petition. Pending that challenge, the Court restrained coercive disconnection of the petitioner's supply if monthly bills were paid, and permitted the licensee to process residents' applications for individual connections, subject to the writ, without hindrance from the petitioner. Clarifying that interim order, the Court held that those applications were for fresh independent connections, not for sub-meters or connections through the existing single-point meter. The writ was later dismissed as withdrawn when counsel did not press it. The validity of the Clause 4.9 amendment was not decided.
facts:
Amity Infra Developers Pvt. Ltd. challenged the amendment of Clause 4.9 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 directing conversion of single-point electricity connections into multiple-point connections. It was a developer with a single-point supply to a building whose residents were applying for individual connections. On 23 April 2019 a Division Bench listed the writ with the similar Writ-C No. 4545 of 2019 (M/s Maxbills Construction Pvt. Ltd.) and, as an interim measure, restrained coercive disconnection if monthly bills were paid, while allowing the respondents to process residents' individual-connection applications, subject to the writ, and directing the petitioner not to hinder those sanctions.

The petitioner sought clarification that the respondents were granting connections through its existing single-point meter, so billing would run through that meter. On 13 May 2019 the same Bench clarified that the 23 April order meant fresh independent connections, not sub-meters. An impleadment by Sri Anshuman Vidhu Chandra was taken on record on 15 May 2019. On 1 December 2021 counsel did not press the writ, and it was dismissed as withdrawn.

holding_units.clause: 4.9 (as amended — conversion of single-point to multiple-point connections)
holding_units.topic: pending a Clause 4.9 conversion challenge, individual resident connections mean independent supply, not sub-meters through the existing single-point meter; writ later withdrawn
holding_units.question: Pending a developer's challenge to the Clause 4.9 amendment converting single-point connections to multiple-point, may the licensee process residents' applications as sub-meters billed through the existing single-point meter?
holding_units.holding: No, as an interim construction of the Court's own 23.4.2019 order. The Court listed the writ with Maxbills Construction, restrained coercive disconnection if monthly bills were paid, and permitted the respondents to process residents' applications for individual connections subject to the writ, the petitioner not to hinder. On the petitioner's complaint that connections were being granted through its meter, the Court clarified on 13.5.2019 that those applications were for fresh independent connections, not for installation of any sub-meter or connection through the existing single-point meter. On 1.12.2021 counsel did not press the writ and it was dismissed as withdrawn. The amendment itself was not decided.
holding_units.qualifier: The 23.4.2019 and 13.5.2019 directions were interlocutory (Pankaj Mithal, J. and Prakash Padia, J.). The writ was dismissed as withdrawn on 1.12.2021 without a merits decision on Clause 4.9.

principle_tags.application: The writ challenged the Clause 4.9 amendment converting single-point connections to multiple-point. The Court listed it with Maxbills Construction and gave interim protection, but counsel later did not press the petition and it was dismissed as withdrawn without deciding the amendment.

Pending the conversion challenge, residents' individual-connection applications were to be processed as fresh independent connections, not as sub-meters or connections through the developer's existing single-point meter. The conversion mandate itself was not adjudicated.

The developer's pending challenge to Clause 4.9, and its existing single-point supply, did not bar the licensee from processing residents' applications for individual connections; the petitioner was directed not to hinder those sanctions.

The 23.4.2019 liberty to process individual applications was clarified on 13.5.2019 to mean fresh independent connections, not installation of a sub-meter or a connection through the existing single-point meter, so that billing would not run through the developer's meter.
